correctness.rationale: Independent sign changes are isometries of the absolute Cesàro \(p=3\) norm, so averaging an arbitrary Euclidean pullback removes the mixed term without weakening its comparison constants. For \(q_r(x,y)=x^2+r y^2\), homogeneity reduces the distortion to the ratio of extrema of \(F_r(t)\). The derivative equation is exactly \(r=R(t)=(1+t)^2/[t((1+t)^2+8)]\); the displayed derivative of \(R\) is negative because \(t^3+3t^2-5t+9=t(t-1)^2+5(t-3/5)^2+36/5>0\). Hence each \(F_r\) has one interior maximum. Equalizing the two endpoint minima gives \(r_0=3^{-4/3}\), and the comparison used in the proof shows every other \(r\) has at least as large a distortion. Fresh numerical replay of the defining scalar equation gave \(	au=2.7667398800787\ldots\), squared distance \(1.2995820436010388\ldots\), and distance \(1.1399921243592162\ldots\), matching the record.
